c1|1.evidence_quote: mean sleep duration among adolescents fell by 18 minutes per night in the pooled sample
c1|1.analysis: The pooled survey data show a decline in adolescent sleep between 1990 and 2010.

c2|2.evidence_quote: participants recalled 30% fewer words the morning after restricted sleep in a field study
c2|2.analysis: FABRICATED on purpose to test the quote check.

c3|3.evidence_quote: In children under 12 we found no association between spindle density and overnight retention.
c3|3.analysis: The source finds no association in children and only a modest one in adults, so the claim about every age group is contradicted.

c6|1.evidence_quote: These findings suggest that adolescents now sleep less than previous generations
c6|1.analysis: Supports less sleep, not that sleep drives learning.

c6|2.evidence_quote: recalled 12% fewer words the next morning than after a night of normal sleep
c6|2.analysis: Lab evidence of lower recall after restricted sleep, in one night only.
